title: Navigation API: Option to treat `sameDocument` traverse as a regular navigation when no `intercept()` is registered

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#289 — filed by @jordanw66 (2025-05). Discussed with @domenic.

---

### The problem

When an app navigates with `intercept()`, it creates `sameDocument` history entries. If those entries are later traversed **in a document where no `intercept()` handler is registered**, nothing happens — the URL changes and the back/forward buttons appear broken.

Ways to end up there, per the original thread:

- user reloads an intercepted URL and the SSR'd page doesn't register a handler
- user cancels the reload, or hits back/forward, before the handler script loads and registers
- intermittent network failure or a stale cache/bundle version prevents the handler loading
- JavaScript is disabled

### The ask

Let the browser treat such traversals — at least those changing path or query — as **regular cross-document navigations** when no handler is registered, instead of silently doing nothing.

### Note on prior discussion

@domenic's response was that this "might be possible, but it would be hard to prioritize a feature that is part of a JavaScript API, and is geared toward an edge-case where the user turns off JavaScript." @jordanw66 pushed back that JS-disabled was a poor example, and the broader failure modes above (network, cache/bundle mismatch, interrupted load, stop/back before handler registration) are ordinary production occurrences rather than edge cases. That reframing was never responded to, so migrating on that basis.

Related: WICG/navigation-api#99 (migrated separately) is the same class of problem approached from the document-swap side.

cc @jordanw66 @domenic
